title: Build a strong tabular baseline
problem: A modest structured dataset and a business prediction target.
rationale: Start with a simple scikit-learn baseline; try CatBoost when categorical features are central. Add Polars only if data manipulation benefits.
first_step: One Python environment, a train/test split appropriate to time or groups, and a reproducible baseline before tuning.
validation: Compare against a dummy predictor on a leakage-safe holdout; record calibration, subgroup error and total development time.
caveat: A tuned deep model is not automatically better on tabular data; categoricals and time leakage need explicit treatment.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Run a private local language model
problem: Model inputs must remain on a machine you control.
rationale: Use llama.cpp for low-level control; Ollama or LM Studio for a more convenient local workflow. These are alternatives, not a required four-tool stack.
first_step: Load one legally usable model that fits your memory, disable unnecessary network integrations, and test a representative prompt.
validation: Measure peak memory, time to first token, tokens per second and answer quality at the actual context length.
caveat: Local execution alone does not secure downloaded models, logs, plug-ins or the surrounding application.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Build local document question answering
problem: A small private document collection with traceable answers.
rationale: Parse documents, embed chunks locally, retrieve with FAISS, then pass evidence to a local model. A persisted database can replace FAISS when updates and access control grow.
first_step: Start with 20 representative documents, explicit chunk IDs and answers that cite exact passages.
validation: Hand-label a small query set; measure retrieval recall, citation support and refusal when evidence is missing.
caveat: Text extraction, permission filtering and retrieval errors can matter more than which language model is largest.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Add RAG to an existing Postgres application
problem: Your application already stores users and permissions in PostgreSQL.
rationale: pgvector can keep vector retrieval next to relational filters; use a hosted model only when privacy and provider terms permit.
first_step: Add a narrow retrieval endpoint to the existing service before introducing a separate vector database or agent framework.
validation: Test retrieval recall and p95 latency with real permission filters; test inaccessible documents never appear in answers or logs.
caveat: An API key and prompt are not access control. Retention, residency and cost need separate review.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested

title: Adapt a small model with limited GPU memory
problem: A specific behavioral task, curated examples and constrained accelerator memory.
rationale: Use adapters to reduce trainable state; add low-bit loading only when the selected model, hardware and optimizer support it.
first_step: First establish a prompt-only baseline; then train a small adapter on a clean split and preserve the exact configuration.
validation: Evaluate held-out task quality, general-capability regression, safety regressions, memory and inference cost.
caveat: Adapter training does not fix poor data, memorization or insufficient base-model capability; quantization support is version-specific.
status: Editorial starting configuration — not end-to-end tested
